profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record, tagged Verizon Branchburg NEC Datacenter, sits on Industrial Parkway in Branchburg Township, Somerset County, New Jersey. New Jersey falls within Verizon nine-state incumbent local exchange carrier footprint inherited from the Bell Atlantic and NYNEX mergers, so a legacy network facility here is geographically plausible. The name includes the abbreviation NEC, which plausibly stands for Network Engineering Center, a facility-naming convention associated with Bell Atlantic and Verizon network operations, though this expansion is inferred from the naming pattern rather than confirmed by any operator source. The telecom=data_center tag was added by the same single contributor, on the same day in August 2026, citing the same local knowledge sourcing used on the nearby Freehold record, which on its own would be weak, unverifiable provenance. Unlike Freehold, however, this Branchburg record has independent corroboration: a separate OpenStreetMap contributor mapped a lattice communications tower on essentially the same building footprint back in 2021, tagged as a mobile-phone communications structure, years before and independently of the 2026 data-center tagging pass. An active communications tower co-located with a building is meaningful supporting evidence that this site carries real telecom transmission or switching function, even though it does not by itself confirm commercial data-center status or specifications. Branchburg and the broader Somerset County corridor have long hosted Bell System and AT&T network facilities given the area role in New Jersey telecom infrastructure history. No capacity, technical square footage, tier rating, or year-built figures are asserted here because no source establishes them, but this record carries somewhat stronger circumstantial support than several others in this Verizon cluster.

profile.research_note: Verizon sold its commercial colocation/data-center business (29 facilities) to Equinix in 2017 and exited the public colocation market; it does not publish colocation spec sheets. These rows are Verizon-operated network facilities (switching centers, wireless MSC/central-office buildings) rather than for-lease colocation space, and no public technical spec page exists for them. Marked specs_unpublished rather than guess.

reading.body:
Verizon Branchburg NEC Datacenter sits in Somerset County on Industrial Parkway in Branchburg Township, New Jersey. No technical specifications are published for this facility. The research indicates this is a network operations center rather than a commercial colocation campus, as Verizon sold its 29 colocation data centers to Equinix in 2017 and no longer publishes specs for its remaining telecom switching facilities. An active communications tower mapped on the same building footprint in 2021, before any data center tagging, independently corroborates that the site carries telecom transmission or switching function, though this does not confirm commercial hosting capacity or power consumption.

New Jersey has 48 mapped data center facilities, of which only 5 publish power capacity figures totaling 111.3 megawatts. Branchburg ranks sixth by published megawatts in the state, which means it either publishes no capacity figure or publishes below the fifth-ranked facility. Somerset County sits within Verizon's incumbent local exchange carrier footprint from the Bell Atlantic and NYNEX mergers, making a legacy network facility plausible in the corridor's telecom infrastructure history. The lack of published capacity means this campus cannot be assessed against the state's published base or counted toward AI infrastructure inventory.

For a reader deciding whether this campus matters to AI, the absence of published specifications makes it invisible to the analysis. Even if Branchburg holds switching or transport infrastructure, network operations centers do not typically host commercial accelerator workloads or count toward grid-constrained AI scaling capacity. The presence of the facility can be noted as mapped, but its relevance to AI depends on whether it serves colocation tenants, a detail the operator does not publish and research has not confirmed.
